frozen_decisions_applied: Plan #8's second sentence, verbatim: 'Verify manufacturing/provisioning uniqueness; duplicate/cloned GatewayId evidence blocks production enrollment.' FD-17, verbatim: 'Manufacturing/provisioning evidence must reject duplicate or cloned GatewayId enrollment.' -- an explicit, documented scoping decision was made rather than force-fitting a fake substitute: fleet-wide duplicate-enrollment detection (across physically different devices) needs a manufacturing backend/fleet registry this project does not have, and depends on the real eFuse burn/attestation workflow (plan #6-#8, S5) already found BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING. Building a 'uniqueness check' with nothing real to check against would verify nothing real -- worse than not building it. Instead, a narrower, still-meaningful LOCAL self-consistency check was built: does the live-read GatewayId match the one recorded once during manufacturing?

This is explicitly NOT the same guarantee as fleet-wide duplicate-enrollment detection -- documented directly in the new module's own header comment and in CONTROL_PLANE_SECURITY.md Section 2.9, not overclaimed.

The manufacturing-recorded GatewayId is stored as a raw 6-byte blob under a new 'mfg_gateway_id' key, deliberately NOT parsed out of the full eFuse-provisioning-template JSON record (manufacturing_provisioning_get_efuse_record(), plan S5 #5) -- parsing JSON on-device today would duplicate plan #24's not-yet-built cJSON-backed StrictJsonObjectReader, which this project's own FD text forbids without a documented unmet product requirement.

Fails closed on every non-match outcome: kNoManufacturingRecord is treated exactly the same as kMismatch by gateway_id_verification_allows_production_enrollment() -- absence of manufacturing evidence is never implicit proof of authenticity. This predicate always returns false in a real deployment today, mirroring provisioning_secret_provider.hpp's own production adapter for the identical missing-manufacturing-material reason.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only a local, single-device self-consistency check is implemented -- fleet-wide duplicate/cloned-GatewayId enrollment detection across physically different devices (the more natural reading of plan #8's 'uniqueness' text and FD-17's 'reject duplicate or cloned GatewayId enrollment') is not built.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Fleet-wide detection needs a manufacturing backend or fleet registry this project's architecture does not include at all (this repository is a single-gateway firmware codebase), and in any case depends on the real eFuse burn/attestation workflow (plan #6-#8, S5) already found BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING. Building a 'uniqueness check' with no real manufacturing backend or attestation to check against would produce a check that verifies nothing real.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: This sub-slice cannot detect two different physical devices claiming the same GatewayId (a genuine cloning/counterfeiting scenario) -- only that THIS device's current live identity matches what was recorded on it during its own manufacturing. Real fleet-wide protection against cloning remains unimplemented and, per the plan's own precondition text, effectively blocked pending real manufacturing infrastructure this project does not have.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The manufacturing-recorded GatewayId is stored as its own separate, simple 6-byte blob ('mfg_gateway_id') rather than extracted from the existing full eFuse-provisioning-template JSON record (manufacturing_provisioning_get_efuse_record(), which already contains a gateway_id field per scripts/efuse_provisioning_template.py's own schema).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Parsing JSON on-device ahead of plan #24's not-yet-built cJSON-backed StrictJsonObjectReader would duplicate that future, centralized work -- this project's own FD text explicitly forbids application code duplicating a platform/parsing primitive without a documented unmet product requirement, and a one-off ad-hoc JSON extraction here would be exactly that.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future real manufacturing/provisioning workflow (plan #6-#8) would need to write to BOTH the existing 'mfg_efuse_rec' JSON blob (for full audit/evidence purposes) AND this new 'mfg_gateway_id' simple blob (for this module's fast, JSON-free comparison) -- a small, deliberate redundancy accepted in exchange for not building a throwaway JSON parser.
